title: Balak: the donkey saw first (Numbers 22:21–35)
hookLine: the donkey sees the angel before the well-known prophet does
tomorrow: Balak: only the word I'm given

lines: THE DOG WON'T GO DOWN THE STAIRS.
THE HIRED SEER ON THE ROAD.
cards: The dog won't go down the stairs. The toddler points at something in the corner of the room. The quiet intern says, I think the numbers are wrong.
It's easy to brush them off; the experts are in charge. Balaam is the expert in this story, a seer a king will pay to see what others can't.
He sets off on the road to Moab, riding his own donkey, the one he's ridden all his life. And on that road, the donkey sees something he doesn't.

teach.h: AN ANGEL WITH A DRAWN SWORD.
teach.b: In paraphrase: an angel of God stands in the road with a drawn sword. The donkey sees it and swerves into a field. Balaam beats her back onto the road.
Then the path narrows between two vineyard walls. The angel stands there, and the donkey presses against the wall and crushes Balaam's foot. He beats her again.
Then a place so narrow there's no way to turn at all. The donkey lies down under him, and Balaam, furious, beats her with his staff. Three times she saw.

teach.h: THREE TIMES SHE SAW, THREE TIMES HE STRUCK.
teach.b: Three times he struck. Then God opens the donkey's mouth, and she asks, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?"
Balaam answers her, as if talking donkeys were normal: you've made a fool of me; if I had a sword in my hand, I'd kill you. The rabbis enjoyed the irony.
A man setting out to destroy a whole nation with his words can't handle his donkey without a sword. Then the donkey asks, gently: haven't I carried you all your life?

teach.h: HAVE I EVER DONE THIS BEFORE?
teach.b: Have I ever done this before? And he has to say no. Only then does God open Balaam's eyes, and he sees the angel.

The Mishnah, in Pirkei Avot, lists the mouth of the donkey among ten things God created at twilight on the eve of the very first Sabbath, as if it had been waiting since creation for this one conversation.
The hired seer saw last. The humble animal saw first, and the best thing it did was ask a question.

how: Balaam's talking donkey is read in synagogue in the portion of Balak, and it is often retold for children, with the donkey's question at the center.

o: the angel who blocked the road with a sword

s: Balaam saw the angel before his donkey did
the donkey saw it three times. Balaam saw only when God opened his eyes.
the Mishnah lists the donkey's mouth among things made on the eve of the first Sabbath
Pirkei Avot 5:6 lists ten things created at twilight.
Balaam was shocked that his donkey could speak

games.q: you're Balaam's donkey. there's an angel with a drawn sword in the road. your rider can't see it. what do you do?
o: walk straight on: he's the expert.
swerve, again and again, even when he strikes you.
games.why: she turned aside three times and took three beatings, until God opened her mouth and then Balaam's eyes.

practice: Think of someone whose warnings you tend to wave away: a child, an older parent, a junior colleague, a friend who's usually quiet.
Imagine them asking you the donkey's question, have I ever steered you wrong before, and let the answer come honestly.
